summary: Verify the 6 structure findings and run the completeness critic for the accessibility audit
logs: Running 6 gap auditors: WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus — chart hover tooltips were never assessed; WCAG 3.2.1/3.2.2 (on-focus / on-input context changes) and 3.2.3/3.2.4 (consistency) — no dimension audited these; WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable — auto-dismissing status messages on fixed timers, never audited; Tauri desktop shell accessibility deltas — minWidth 800 + no browser zoom, prefers-* propagation, desktop-only updater states; no audit dimension covered the desktop shell; App states never exercised at runtime: dark-theme axe scan, open-overlay/narrow-nav sub-states, first-run/no-data variants of every tab, zero-result filter states — plus WeatherTideSection.tsx, the one component no audit file mentions; WCAG 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (map pan/pinch alternatives, empirical keyboard-handler check) plus 2.5.4 Motion Actuation and 1.3.4 Orientation confirmation — flagged 'likely fine' but never audited

structureVerdicts.reasoning: Verified: no skip link exists anywhere in src/ or index.html; header (App.tsx:570) has no focusable elements, both TabNav modes are one tab stop, and <main> (App.tsx:586) provides a landmark, so 2.4.1 is technically satisfied (ARIA11) and the cost is one extra Tab. The auditor honestly framed it as a best-practice gap and rated it minor, which is correct — landmarks help AT users but not sighted keyboard users, so a skip link is the standard remaining piece. Fairly-flagged polish item, not pedantry.
structureVerdicts.fixNote: Suggested fix is sound; style .sr-skip-link with var(--sr-*) tokens added to both :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css (per the theming convention), and z-index above 1200 as noted since the map fullscreen overlay and dropdown both sit at 1200.

structureVerdicts.reasoning: All four citations verified: role="tablist" on the <nav> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) overrides its implicit navigation role, so desktop mode exposes no navigation landmark; collapsed mode's wrapper (TabNav.tsx:228) is a bare div with none either; the branding header (App.tsx:570) is a plain div outside any landmark; HelpDocs.tsx:347 is an unlabeled <nav>. Screen-reader landmark navigation therefore cannot locate the primary navigation in either mode — a genuine 1.3.1-adjacent structural gap, distinct from confirmed #33 (which is about dangling tabpanel aria-labelledby, not landmark exposure). Moderate is fair given main and contentinfo exist but the primary nav is unfindable by landmark.
structureVerdicts.fixNote: Fix is correct (nav wrapping a div[role=tablist] is the canonical pattern). Use the same accessible name (e.g. aria-label="Main navigation") on both the desktop and collapsed-mode <nav> wrappers so the landmark announces identically across modes; keep the sr-header className when converting the header div to <header>.

structureVerdicts.reasoning: Duplicate of confirmed finding #33 (TabNav.tsx collapsed dropdown orphans every tabpanel / dangling aria-labelledby). Code verified — App.tsx:588-590 panels reference tab-* ids that exist only while the collapsed dropdown is open (TabNav.tsx:69-73, 297-298) — but this is the same issue at the same root cause; the ancillary aria-activedescendant note is part of the same collapsed-dropdown ARIA wiring, not a separate user-facing defect.

Verified: index.html:7 title is static, no document.title writes anywhere in frontend/src, no routing, and tauri.conf.json:14 hardcodes the window title. Not a 2.4.2 conformance failure (single page, no navigations) but a fairly-flagged SPA best-practice item with real if small orientation benefit for screen-reader users and tab/window switchers across ten distinct views. Severity minor is correct; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
structureVerdicts.fixNote: The useEffect-on-activeTab setting document.title is right for web, but the claim that it 'also updates the desktop window title in Tauri' is wrong — Tauri v2 does not sync document.title to the native window title. Behind isTauri() also call getCurrentWindow().setTitle(...) from @tauri-apps/api/window, and add core:window:allow-set-title to src-tauri/capabilities/default.json (core:default does not include set-title).

structureVerdicts.reasoning: Verified by grep: exactly 43 target="_blank" anchors across 20 component files, with only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 announcing '(opens in new tab)'; HelpDocs.tsx renders every documentation link target="_blank" with no indication and SpeciesLinks.tsx aria-labels omit it. This is the new-window-indication aspect, explicitly distinct from confirmed #53 (which covers the ↗ links' accessible names), so not a duplicate. Correctly scoped as advisory (G201; 3.2.5 is AAA), so minor severity is right; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
structureVerdicts.fixNote: A shared external-link component is sound; prefer a visually-hidden span suffix over aria-label so existing link text is preserved, and where an aria-label already exists (SpeciesLinks, icon-only links) append to the label, matching the wording already used at App.tsx:748/898. For icon-only favicon links keep title in sync with the label.

structureVerdicts.reasoning: This is a merged finding: part (1) — the bare ↗ checklist links in BirdingStats (verified at 1332, 1564, 1589, title="Open checklist" only) — is a duplicate of confirmed finding #53 (same elements, same root cause: inadequate accessible naming of the repeated ↗ links). Part (2) is real and distinct: App.tsx:1101-1110 footer link with text 'SnowRaven' navigates to the GitHub repo with nothing in the text or contentinfo context revealing the destination, while App.tsx:898 already demonstrates the correct pattern for the SnowRaven Mini link. Confirmed on the footer-link aspect only; minor severity fits a single ambiguous 2.4.4 link.
structureVerdicts.fixNote: Treat the ↗-naming portion as covered by confirmed #53 and fix only the footer here: give the footer anchor aria-label="SnowRaven on GitHub (opens in new tab)" (or change the visible text), matching the existing SnowRaven Mini pattern at App.tsx:898.

gapFindings.title: Chart hover tooltips are not hoverable (1.4.13): cursor-following wrapper with pointer-events none on all five recharts Tooltip mounts
gapFindings.wcag: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus AA (failure F95 — content on hover not hoverable)
gapFindings.description: All five recharts <Tooltip> mounts — BirdingStats.tsx:575 and :601 (life-list accumulation area charts), :1276 (checklists-by-observer bar chart), :1768 (media-over-time line chart), and MediaStatsSections.tsx:320 (media-by-hour stacked bar chart) — pass only contentStyle/formatter/labelFormatter, so recharts 3.8.1 defaults apply (trigger 'hover', no fixed position, no wrapperStyle). The library renders the tooltip in a wrapper hardcoded to pointerEvents:'none' that follows the cursor at a ~10px offset (node_modules/recharts/es6/component/TooltipBoundingBox.js:77), so the pointer can never be moved over the tooltip content: approaching it repositions the box and swaps its data to a different point, and at the plot edge the move exits the hover area and the tooltip vanishes. That fails 1.4.13's hoverable condition, which exists for screen-magnification users who must bring revealed content under the lens to read it — the media chart's five-line tooltip in particular can extend past a 400% lens and cannot be panned to without the content changing. The other two 1.4.13 conditions PASS in this recharts version (verified in installed source, see passes), which bounds the severity, as does the trigger-adjacent placement; and because every chart wrapper is role="img" with an aria-label summary, this is a sighted-pointer-user issue only (per-point values are otherwise unavailable as visible text anywhere in the UI). The tooltip is also clamped inside the chart viewBox (allowEscapeViewBox default false), so it can overlay bars, axis ticks, and the media chart's in-container legend — acceptable under 1.4.13 only because the Escape dismissal works. ACCESSIBILITY.md makes no claim about hover content, so this is an undisclosed gap rather than a false statement.
gapFindings.evidence: BirdingStats.tsx:575-582/:601-605/:1276-1280/:1768-1773 and MediaStatsSections.tsx:320-323 pass no content/trigger/position/wrapperStyle props; recharts 3.8.1 TooltipBoundingBox.js:77 sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` in positionStyle and translates the box from the live cursor coordinate via getTooltipTranslate; defaultTooltipProps in Tooltip.js:36-58 sets `trigger: 'hover'`.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Pick one per-chart approach and apply it to all five mounts: (a) anchor the tooltip with a fixed `position={{ x, y }}` (e.g. a chart corner) plus `wrapperStyle={{ pointerEvents: 'auto' }}` — wrapperStyle is spread after the hardcoded style so it wins — making the box stationary and physically hoverable; or (b) switch to `trigger="click"` (supported in recharts 3), which makes the content activation-triggered and exempt from 1.4.13 entirely, matching the posture the app already takes for map popups; or (c) surface the per-point values in a visible-text alternative (a small data-table disclosure under each chart). Mention chart tooltips in ACCESSIBILITY.md once fixed.

verdict.reasoning: All five Tooltip mounts (BirdingStats.tsx:575/601/1276/1768, MediaStatsSections.tsx:320) pass only contentStyle/formatter/labelFormatter, and the installed recharts 3.8.1 hardcodes pointerEvents:'none' plus cursor-following translate in TooltipBoundingBox.js and trigger:'hover' in defaultTooltipProps — so the hover content can never be hovered, an F95 failure of 1.4.13. The bounding claims also check out: Escape dismissal exists in TooltipBoundingBox, every chart wrapper is role=img with an aria-label, and wrapperStyle is spread after the hardcoded positionStyle so fix option (a) works. No existing finding covers 1.4.13/chart tooltips and ACCESSIBILITY.md says nothing about hover content.
verdict.fixNote: Option (a) is verified workable in the installed source: outerStyle = {...positionStyle, visibility..., ...props.wrapperStyle}, so wrapperStyle={{ pointerEvents: 'auto' }} wins, but it only satisfies 1.4.13 combined with a fixed position prop (otherwise the box still tracks the cursor). Option (b) trigger="click" is the lowest-risk route and matches the app's map-popup posture.

gapFindings.title: Breeding-code meanings are hover-only: full code labels live solely in title attributes on the Breeding Codes tab and comparer badges
gapFindings.wcag: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus AA (UA-tooltip exemption applies — flagged as the only route to the information)
gapFindings.description: Title-attribute tooltips are user-agent controlled and therefore exempt from 1.4.13 itself, but three locations make the title the ONLY route to what an eBird breeding code abbreviation means, and UA title tooltips never appear on keyboard focus or touch: (1) BreedingCodeTable.tsx:148 — the matrix column headers show only the code (e.g. "NY") with `title={def.label}`; the per-cell sr-only text (line 228) adds only the tier category ("Confirmed"), not the label. (2) BreedingCodeList.tsx:324 — the per-code filter pills, same pattern (`title={def.label}` with the bare code as content). (3) ChecklistComparer.tsx:31-40 — BreedingBadge renders only `def.code` with `title={`${def.code} — ${def.label}`}` and no aria-label. There is no visible legend on the Breeding Codes tab, and docs/HELP.md's Breeding Codes section (line 273+) describes the matrix without listing the 23 codes; the full labels are visible only in Species Detail's per-species breeding section (SpeciesDetail.tsx:~1003), which covers just the codes that one selected species has. Mouse users get the UA tooltip and screen readers get the title as accessible description (name-from-content is the code, title falls back to description), but a sighted keyboard or touch user — including anyone on the self-hosted/tablet path — has no way on these views to learn that "FL" means recently fledged young.
gapFindings.evidence: BreedingCodeTable.tsx:148 `title={def.label}` on a <th> whose visible content is `{code}{sortIndicator(code)}`; BreedingCodeList.tsx:324 `title={def.label}` on the code pill whose content is a color dot + `{code}`; ChecklistComparer.tsx:31 `title={`${def.code} — ${def.label}`}` on a span containing only `{def.code}`; grep finds no other rendering of def.label in those three files and no code legend in docs/HELP.md.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Add a non-hover route on the Breeding Codes tab: a collapsible "Code legend" disclosure above the matrix listing code → label (one shared component could also serve the comparer), or render the label in each column header at reduced size. Minimal alternative: append the label to each control's accessible name (aria-label={`${code} — ${def.label}`} on the pills/headers, keeping the visible code) and give ChecklistComparer's BreedingBadge the same aria-label — that fixes AT consistency, though a visible legend is what helps sighted touch/keyboard users.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at all three locations: BreedingCodeTable.tsx:148 (th content is just the code, title={def.label}; the per-cell sr-only at :228 adds only the tier category), BreedingCodeList.tsx:324 (pill with title only), and ChecklistComparer.tsx:31 (BreedingBadge, title only — on a non-interactive span, so even AT exposure is unreliable). grep confirms def.label renders nowhere else in those views, docs/HELP.md's Breeding Codes section lists no codes and its comparer section literally says 'Hover for the full code name', and full labels appear only in Species Detail's per-species section. ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'hidden text label' claim covers tier color, not code meaning, so nothing is disclosed; no existing finding overlaps (the confirmed breeding-code items are contrast-only).

gapFindings.title: Species combobox erases the in-progress typed query (and displayed value) on every refocus
gapFindings.wcag: 3.2.1 On Focus (A) — advisory; no conformance failure (usability/data-loss)
gapFindings.description: The species selector's onFocus handler (SpeciesDetail.tsx:481-485) runs setSelectorQuery(''), setActiveOptionIdx(-1), setDropdownOpen(true). Judged against 3.2.1: this is NOT a change of context — focus stays in the input, nothing navigates, no focus is moved elsewhere, and opening the component's own listbox below the input is an accepted combobox auto-expand pattern (the persistent species selection and the page content beneath are untouched, since selectorDisplayValue at :400-402 only swaps between query and selected name). The conformance verdict is therefore PASS, but the query wipe is a real usability defect that lands hardest on keyboard, screen-reader, and screen-magnifier users: type a partial search (e.g. 'warb'), Tab or Shift+Tab away to check a filter, return to the input — the typed text is silently discarded, the input goes blank, and the listbox resets to the full unfiltered species list. Pointer users who click back into the field mid-edit lose their query the same way. There is no announcement that the value changed. Tab already closes the dropdown (:488), so the refocus wipe is not needed for that flow.
gapFindings.evidence: SpeciesDetail.tsx:481-485 `onFocus={() => { setSelectorQuery(''); setActiveOptionIdx(-1); setDropdownOpen(true) }}`; display value at :400-402 `const selectorDisplayValue = dropdownOpen ? selectorQuery : (selectedSpecies ?? '')`.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Stop clearing the query on focus: keep onFocus={() => { setDropdownOpen(true) }} so the prior query (and its filtered list) is restored on refocus, and select the input's text instead (e.currentTarget.select()) so a user who wants a fresh search can just start typing to replace it. Reset the query only on explicit selection or Escape, where it already happens (:487, :501).

verdict.reasoning: Code matches exactly: SpeciesDetail.tsx:481-485 onFocus runs setSelectorQuery('') before opening the dropdown, and the display value at :400-402 swaps to the now-empty query, so a partial search typed before tabbing away (Tab keeps selectorQuery intact at :488) is silently wiped on refocus. The 3.2.1-passes analysis is correct and the advisory framing is honest, but the silent data loss is real and lands hardest on keyboard/SR/magnifier users, so it is not pedantry. Distinct from confirmed #29 (Escape strands focus on body) — different handler, different defect.

gapFindings.title: The same 'open this checklist on eBird' function is identified four different ways across tabs
gapFindings.description: One repeated function — a link that opens a specific checklist on ebird.org — is identified with four different affordances and three different name vocabularies depending on the tab (this is the identification inconsistency itself, distinct from the already-reported missing new-window indication and the ↗ accessible-name weakness): (1) bare '↗' glyph with title="Open checklist" (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589); (2) data value + lucide ExternalLink icon, no label at all (speciesDetail/ui.tsx:52-78 StatValueLink, Checklists.tsx:48-65 DateLink) — except NamedBirdRow.tsx:91-100, where the identical id+icon link carries aria-label="Open eBird checklist S… (opens in a new tab)"; (3) plain accent-colored text with no icon and no underline, indistinguishable from the adjacent non-link values (BirdingStats.tsx:500, 695, 726, 1448, 1525; SightingsMap.tsx:67 popup dates; map/TargetMarkers.tsx:104); (4) underlined id text with title="View this checklist on eBird" (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). Where a name exists it is inconsistent F31-style: "Open checklist" vs "View this checklist on eBird" vs "Open eBird checklist S…". A screen-reader user who learns one identification on the Checklists tab cannot recognize the same function on Statistics or in a map popup, and sighted users get no stable visual signature for 'this opens the checklist' either.
gapFindings.evidence: WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111 `{id}` vs BirdingStats.tsx:1332 `↗` vs Checklists.tsx:54-62 `{formatDate(date)}` (no label) vs BirdingStats.tsx:500-505 date-only link with `textDecoration: 'none'` and no icon.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Create one shared ChecklistLink component (extending the existing speciesDetail/ui.tsx StatValueLink, which already gates on SUBMISSION_ID_RE) with a single visual signature (ExternalLink icon) and one accessible-name formula (e.g. aria-label=`Open checklist ${id} on eBird` plus the new-tab suffix already used in NamedBirdRow). Replace all four variants — the ↗ glyphs, the unlabeled icon links, the plain-text links, and the title-only underlined ids — with it.

verdict.reasoning: All four variants verified at the cited lines: bare ↗ with title='Open checklist' (BirdingStats 1332/1564/1589), value+ExternalLink with no label (StatValueLink ui.tsx:52-78, DateLink Checklists.tsx:48-65) vs NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100's full aria-label, plain accent text with textDecoration:'none' (BirdingStats 500/695/726/1448/1525, SightingsMap.tsx:62-75, TargetMarkers.tsx:104 — which is in fact a fifth vocabulary, 'View checklist S… →'), and underlined id with title='View this checklist on eBird' (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). This is a genuine 3.2.4 inconsistent-identification issue whose root cause (no shared component or name formula) is distinct from confirmed #53 (↗ missing accessible name) and structure findings #4/#5 (new-window indication, title-attribute reliance), which the finding explicitly carves out. The suggested shared ChecklistLink keeps the SUBMISSION_ID_RE standing security check, consistent with conventions.

gapFindings.title: Date-range filter is a native date picker on four tabs but free-text 'YYYY-MM-DD' fields on Map Explorer
gapFindings.wcag: 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA) — advisory; primarily a consistency/usability gap
gapFindings.description: The identical 'filter sightings by date range' function is presented and identified two different ways. Life List (LifeList.tsx:644-669), Breeding Codes (BreedingCodeList.tsx:408-419), Species Detail (SpeciesDetail.tsx:629-654), and Checklists (Checklists.tsx:653-667) all use paired <input type="date"> controls — native picker UI, a Calendar icon, an accent-fill active state, and a '→' separator. Map Explorer alone implements the same function as two <input type="text"> fields whose only identification is the placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD' (MapExplorer.tsx:862-865), under a 'Date Range' sidebar label. A user who has learned the app-wide date-picker idiom reaches the map and must instead hand-type ISO dates with no picker, no format validation affordance, and no visible from/to distinction (the indistinguishable naming is already reported; this finding is the cross-tab inconsistency of widget and identification). The interaction divergence is not a strict 3.2.4 failure (3.2.4 governs identification, and the labels that do exist don't conflict), so this is recorded as an advisory consistency defect with real cognitive-accessibility cost.
gapFindings.evidence: MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 `<input type="text" placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" value={dateFrom} …/><input type="text" placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" value={dateTo} …/>` vs LifeList.tsx:644-647 `<input type="date" value={dateRange.from} …/>` (same pattern on BreedingCodeList.tsx:408, SpeciesDetail.tsx:629, Checklists.tsx:653).
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Switch the Map Explorer sidebar date fields to the same paired <input type="date"> pattern used everywhere else (with the From/To accessible names the prior audit already calls for); keep the visible 'Date Range' SidebarLabel, which the other tabs could in fact adopt.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 uses two <input type="text"> with only a 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder under one 'Date Range' label, while LifeList.tsx:644, BreedingCodeList.tsx:408, SpeciesDetail.tsx:629, and Checklists.tsx:653 all use paired <input type="date"> (one evidence overstatement: Checklists' pair has no Calendar icon or accent-fill active state — those three trimmings are on the other three tabs only, but the core text-vs-native-picker divergence holds). The advisory framing is fair — same function, different widget and identification, with real cognitive/motor cost from hand-typing ISO dates. Distinct aspect and fix from confirmed #56/#59, which cover the accessible-name/placeholder problem on the same inputs.
verdict.fixNote: Switching to type="date" also moots the 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder-as-name issue from #56/#59 — apply the From/To aria-labels (as Checklists.tsx:655/663 already does) in the same change.

gapFindings.title: Footer update-checker outcomes auto-dismiss on fixed 4–8s timers with no way to extend — including the web path's actionable 'update available' instruction
gapFindings.description: Every outcome of the user-initiated 'Check For Updates' action is erased by a content-set time limit with no mechanism to turn off, adjust, or extend it (none of the 2.2.1 exceptions — real-time, essential, 20-hour — applies). Worst case: on the WEB path, the 'available' state renders 'v{latest} available — run ./update.sh' (App.tsx:1172-1177) — actionable content the user must read, remember, and carry to a terminal — and auto-reverts to idle after 8000ms (App.tsx:505). The Tauri path proves persistence is the intended design: its 'available' state (App.tsx:492-493) has NO timer and keeps its Install button indefinitely, so the web timer is an arbitrary asymmetry. Additionally, 'up-to-date' ('Up to date (v{current})' — the answer to the user's question, shown nowhere else) and 'error' ('Could not check for updates') auto-revert after 4000ms (App.tsx:491, 496, 502, 510; the post-install failure at 524), after which the footer returns to the bare 'Check For Updates' button — indistinguishable from never having clicked. A screen-magnifier user panning the viewport, a user reading at 200% text size, or a user with a cognitive disability can entirely miss a 4-second message, and because the timer re-arms on every check, re-clicking the button is not an extension mechanism — the reading window can never exceed 8 seconds. This compounds verified finding i=35 (the 'available' and 'error' states are also never announced to AT): for a screen-reader user the error outcome is both silent AND gone within 4 seconds. Applying the brief-success-confirmation reasoning explicitly: only 'up-to-date' resembles a success confirmation, and even it carries content (the version number) with no persistent equivalent; 'available' and 'error' are informational/actionable outcomes, not confirmations, so the commonly-accepted toast exemption does not cover them.
gapFindings.evidence: App.tsx:505 `updateTimerRef.current = setTimeout(() => setUpdateStatus({ kind: 'idle' }), 8000)` on the web 'available' branch, whose render (App.tsx:1173-1175) is 'v{updateStatus.latest} available — run ./update.sh'; the Tauri 'available' branch at 492-493 sets state with no timer; 'up-to-date'/'error' timers at 491, 496, 502, 510, 524 all revert to {kind:'idle'} after 4000ms, unmounting the message span (renders at 1153-1154, 1190-1192).
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Remove the auto-revert timers for the 'available' (web) and 'error' states — let them persist until the user acts, exactly as the Tauri 'available' state already does (render the 'Check For Updates' button alongside or convert the message to include a dismiss/recheck affordance). For 'up-to-date', either let it persist with the recheck button returning next to it, or keep an auto-revert only if the duration is generous (20s+) — though persisting is simpler and costs nothing in a footer. This pairs naturally with the fix for verified finding i=35: one persistent aria-live span whose text changes per state, with the timer logic deleted rather than announced.

verdict.reasoning: All six timers verified at App.tsx:491/496/502/510/524 (4000ms) and :505 (8000ms on the web 'available' branch, whose render at 1173-1176 contains the actionable './update.sh' instruction); the Tauri 'available' branch (492-493) persists indefinitely, proving the asymmetry. No 2.2.1 exception applies and re-clicking is not an Extend mechanism (each window stays ≤8s, no warning, <20s); the 'up-to-date' answer and the error message vanish in 4s leaving the footer indistinguishable from never having clicked. Distinct root cause (content-set time limits, 2.2.1) from confirmed i=35 (live-region semantics, 4.1.3) and absent from both findings files, so not a duplicate; moderate is fair given it compounds i=35 on the same user-initiated flow.
verdict.fixNote: Delete the timers for 'available' (web) and 'error' and let them persist like the Tauri 'available' branch; re-render the 'Check For Updates' button alongside the persistent message (also resolving the idle-button unmount focus drop noted under i=28). Fold into i=35's fix: one always-mounted aria-live span whose text changes per state, timer logic removed rather than announced.

gapFindings.title: Desktop: no page-zoom path exists — Ctrl/Cmd+= is a no-op and the window floor is 800 CSS px, so the 1.4.10 reflow condition is unreachable and ACCESSIBILITY.md's zoom sentence is false on desktop
gapFindings.wcag: 1.4.10 Reflow AA (WCAG2ICT) / 1.4.4 Resize Text AA — plus published-claim accuracy
gapFindings.description: The main window sets minWidth: 800 (tauri.conf.json:17) and does NOT set zoomHotkeysEnabled, which defaults to false (verified in the repo's own @tauri-apps/cli config.schema.json: WindowConfig.zoomHotkeysEnabled, "default": false — on Windows it controls WebView2's IsZoomControlEnabled, i.e. Ctrl+hotkey AND Ctrl+wheel zoom; on macOS/Linux it injects a JS polyfill). No Rust code wires any menu, accelerator, or zoom command (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:48-68 registers only plugins and 5 commands; main.rs is 6 lines), and capabilities/default.json lacks the webview:allow-set-webview-zoom permission the macOS/Linux polyfill would require even if enabled. Net effect, derived statically: in the desktop app, Ctrl/Cmd +/−/wheel zoom does nothing on any platform, and the window can never present narrower than 800 CSS px. Consequences under WCAG2ICT reasoning: (1) the web audit's 1.4.10 verification at 320 CSS px and its 1.4.4 verification via browser zoom are both unreachable on desktop — the only enlargement mechanism is the in-app Text Size control capped at 200% (lib/textScale.ts:11, TEXT_SCALES max 2). That satisfies SC 1.4.4's 200% requirement, but the 400%-equivalent enlarged view SC 1.4.10 presupposes (1280px viewport at 400% = 320 CSS px) can never be produced, so the desktop product conforms to 1.4.10 only vacuously, and a desktop low-vision user who needs more than 2x enlargement has no in-app path at all (a web user has browser zoom to 400%+, stackable with Text Size). OS display scaling enlarges physical pixels but cannot push the window below 800 CSS px either. (2) ACCESSIBILITY.md:39 states "Browser/page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too" within a statement that explicitly covers the desktop app (line 3: "It runs in the browser and as a desktop app") — that sentence is false on desktop, and it sits two lines below line 37's own correct disclosure that the desktop app "has no browser zoom of its own", an internal contradiction. Status: the config default is documented and there is zero zoom wiring anywhere in src-tauri, so this is asserted statically; a live desktop run to confirm the hotkeys are inert is advisable (needs-runtime-verification as a formality only).
gapFindings.evidence: tauri.conf.json:12-19 window config contains only title/width/height/minWidth/minHeight; node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/config.schema.json WindowConfig.zoomHotkeysEnabled → "default": false, macOS/Linux polyfill "Requires `webview:allow-set-webview-zoom` permission"; src-tauri/capabilities/default.json has no webview:* permission; ACCESSIBILITY.md:39 "Browser/page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too." vs :37 "the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own".
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Set "zoomHotkeysEnabled": true on the main window in tauri.conf.json and add "webview:allow-set-webview-zoom" to capabilities/default.json — Tauri then provides Ctrl/Cmd +/− page zoom from 20% to 1000% on all three desktop platforms, giving the desktop product a real 1.4.10/1.4.4 path (verify on a live build, especially the macOS/Linux polyfill). gapFindings.title: Desktop updater: download progress has no progressbar semantics and mutates a polite live region on every network chunk; the flow ends in an unannounced self-restart ('ready-to-restart' is dead UI set after relaunch() has begun)
gapFindings.wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A / 4.1.3 Status Messages AA (3.2.2 advisory)
gapFindings.description: Desktop-only updater states beyond verified-finding i=35's scope (which covered only the unreliable mount-with-text announcement of checking/up-to-date/downloading and the missing announcements for 'available'/'error' — not re-reported here): (1) No progressbar semantics: the 'downloading' state (App.tsx:1179-1186) conveys progress purely as text ("Downloading… N%") in an aria-live="polite" span, with no role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin/max, or aria-busy — AT cannot query the operation's progress as a value. (2) Unthrottled live-region churn: handleInstallUpdate's callback (App.tsx:518-520) calls setUpdateStatus on EVERY 'Progress' chunk event from update.downloadAndInstall (lib/tauri/updateManager.ts:36-42), so the live region's text content mutates dozens-to-hundreds of times across a multi-megabyte universal-bundle download; polite regions queue each text change, so VoiceOver/NVDA either chatter stale percentages for the entire download or coalesce unpredictably. (3) The terminal state is imperceivable: updateManager.downloadAndInstall() awaits relaunch() — which terminates the process — BEFORE returning (updateManager.ts:49-50), so setUpdateStatus({kind:'ready-to-restart'}) at App.tsx:521 runs only as the process is already exiting; the "Update installed — restarting…" span (App.tsx:1187-1189) is statically dead UI, and even if it paints for a frame it carries no live semantics. The resulting SR experience: "Downloading… 97%", then the application silently quits and relaunches with no completion message and no prior notice — the trigger is labeled only "Install update" (App.tsx:1169), nothing warns of the immediate automatic restart. Additional note, NOT counted as a new finding: the 'idle' "Check For Updates" button (App.tsx:1129-1146) and the "Install update" button unmount on activation, dropping keyboard focus to <body> — two further locations of the unmount-on-activation pattern already recorded as verified-finding i=28, whose location list omits the footer. needs-runtime-verification: whether the 'ready-to-restart' frame ever paints before process exit, and the actual VoiceOver/NVDA behavior on the per-chunk live updates.
gapFindings.evidence: App.tsx:1180-1185 `<span aria-live="polite">…{updateStatus.progress !== null ? `Downloading… ${Math.round(updateStatus.progress * 100)}%` : 'Downloading update…'}` (no progressbar role); App.tsx:518-520 setUpdateStatus inside the per-chunk onProgress; updateManager.ts:36-43 onProgress fires per 'Progress' event, :49-50 `const { relaunch } = await import('@tauri-apps/plugin-process'); await relaunch();` before the function returns; App.tsx:1187-1189 plain span with no live attributes.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Give the downloading indicator role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin={0} aria-valuemax={100} aria-valuenow={Math.round(progress*100)} (and aria-label="Downloading update"), and throttle state/announcement updates (e.g. update only when the rounded percent crosses a 5-10% step, or announce milestones at 25/50/75/100 via the single persistent polite live region that finding i=35 already recommends for the footer). Announce intent up front: on Install activation, push "Downloading update — SnowRaven will restart automatically when finished" into that live region, and/or rename the button "Install update and restart". If a perceivable completion state is wanted, split relaunch() out of downloadAndInstall(): set 'ready-to-restart', announce it assertively, then call relaunch() after a short delay.

verdict.reasoning: All three sub-claims verified in code: the 'downloading' span (App.tsx:1180-1185) is a text-only aria-live region with no progressbar role/values; setUpdateStatus fires on every 'Progress' chunk (App.tsx:518-520, updateManager.ts:36-42) so the polite region's text mutates per network chunk; and updateManager.ts:49-50 awaits relaunch() — which exits the process — before returning, making the 'ready-to-restart' state at App.tsx:521 and its non-live span (1187-1189) statically dead, so the app silently quits at ~100% with the trigger labeled only 'Install update'. Genuinely distinct from confirmed i=35 (announcement reliability of mounted spans, not value semantics, churn, or the restart) and from i=70 (keystroke churn at a different location); not in either findings file. Moderate is right: a screen-reader user gets chatter then an unexplained app disappearance on a desktop-critical flow.
verdict.fixNote: Fix is sound and convention-compatible: add role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin/max/now, throttle updates to ~5% steps, announce the impending automatic restart up front (or rename the button 'Install update and restart'), and optionally split relaunch() out of downloadAndInstall() so App can set/announce 'ready-to-restart' before relaunching — CLAUDE.md only requires relaunch() (not exit(0)) after downloadAndInstall returns, which this preserves. Route announcements through the single persistent live span from i=35's fix.

gapFindings.title: prefers-reduced-motion propagation into the desktop webviews is platform-dependent and unverified, with no in-app fallback — ACCESSIBILITY.md's unconditional reduced-motion promise rests entirely on it (Linux/WebKitGTK explicitly unconfirmed)
gapFindings.wcag: Published-claim accuracy (ACCESSIBILITY.md:45); 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA — advisory; WCAG 2.2 delta context)
gapFindings.description: Every motion-suppression mechanism in the app depends on the OS setting reaching the embedded webview's (prefers-reduced-motion) media query: the document-wide kill switch (globals.css:588-594), the smoothScrollIntoView guard (lib/scroll.ts:12-18), and the boot-spinner rule (index.html:23). Theme similarly depends on (prefers-color-scheme) (lib/theme.ts:12; index.html anti-flash :39). Per-platform, from code plus documented webview behavior — all marked needs-runtime-verification except macOS: (a) macOS WKWebView (primary shipped platform): both queries are fed from System Settings (Reduce Motion; appearance) — reliable, long-established WebKit behavior. (b) Windows WebView2 (shipped via CI): prefers-reduced-motion maps from Windows Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects → "Animation effects" through Chromium, and prefers-color-scheme from the default app mode via WebView2's PreferredColorScheme (default Auto on current Evergreen runtimes; older runtimes notoriously pinned it light — WebView2Feedback #1779) — expected to work on current runtimes but unverified on the shipped build. (c) Linux WebKitGTK — the case the motion audit explicitly left unverified: WebKitGTK derives prefers-reduced-motion from GtkSettings gtk-enable-animations and prefers-color-scheme from gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme; whether GNOME/KDE accessibility and dark-mode toggles actually reach a Tauri GTK app varies by desktop environment, portal, and theme. (Mitigating scope note: Linux is buildable — bundle.targets "all" — but is not an officially released artifact; releases are macOS via release.sh and Windows via CI.) The asymmetry that makes this an app defect rather than purely a platform caveat: theme and text size both have explicit in-app overrides persisted through the storage seam, but motion has none — grep of Settings.tsx finds no reduce-motion setting, so on any platform where the query fails to propagate, a motion-sensitive user has zero recourse, while ACCESSIBILITY.md:45 promises unconditionally: "If your operating system is set to reduce motion, SnowRaven honors it." The theme equivalent is lower-impact for the same reason in reverse: if prefers-color-scheme fails to propagate, the user still gets the explicit Light/Dark setting (Settings.tsx applyTheme/persistThemePreference), at worst with a wrong-theme first paint on desktop because localStorage is wiped per relaunch and hydration from the storage seam is async (index.html:36-43 → App.tsx:350-354).
gapFindings.evidence: lib/scroll.ts:12-18 and globals.css:588 are the only reduced-motion hooks, both matchMedia/media-query based; `grep -rni reduce frontend/src/components/Settings.tsx` returns nothing (no in-app motion setting); lib/theme.ts:12 matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'); ACCESSIBILITY.md:45 unconditional claim; CLAUDE.md/release.sh: shipped desktop targets are macOS + Windows only.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Add an in-app "Reduce motion" preference (System / Reduced) beside the existing Theme and Text Size controls, persisted via storage.setSetting and applied as a data-reduced-motion attribute on <html> that both the globals.css kill block (duplicate the rules under [data-reduced-motion="reduce"]) and prefersReducedMotion() honor — this makes the ACCESSIBILITY.md promise true regardless of webview propagation. Verify the media queries once on a live Windows (WebView2) build; if a Linux build is ever released, verify under GNOME and KDE. If any gap is confirmed and not fixed, scope ACCESSIBILITY.md line 45 accordingly (per CLAUDE.md, update it in the same change as any behavior change).

verdict.reasoning: The verifiable facts (media-query-only motion suppression in globals.css:588-594/scroll.ts, no in-app reduce-motion setting) check out, but the finding locates no actual defect: relying on prefers-reduced-motion is the standard, recommended implementation, all three webview engines implement the query (WKWebView, Chromium/WebView2, WebKitGTK via gtk-enable-animations), the only verified platform (macOS, the primary shipped target) is conceded reliable, and Linux is not a released artifact. The alleged ACCESSIBILITY.md:45 inaccuracy rests entirely on a hypothetical propagation failure for which no evidence is presented, and reduced motion is AAA (2.3.3) — no WCAG 2.1 AA impact exists. The proposed in-app override is a reasonable enhancement, not the fix for a demonstrated barrier; this is speculative platform-caveat material, not a code finding.

gapFindings.title: WeatherTideSection 'Load weather & tide' button unmounts itself on activation — keyboard focus drops to <body> and its Loading/disabled rendering is dead code
gapFindings.wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (also 4.1.3 Status Messages AA)
gapFindings.description: This component is mentioned by zero prior audit artifacts. The single Load action sets `setLoaded(true)` synchronously as its first statement (line 95), and the header renders the button only while `!keysMissing && !loaded` (line 116) — so the moment a keyboard user presses Enter on it, the focused button unmounts and the browser drops focus to <body> (the user restarts tabbing from the top of the document). Consequently the `disabled={loading}` (117), the `Loader2` spinner, and the `loading ? 'Loading…'` label (124-125) can never render: the button is gone before `loading` is ever true at render time. The loading announcement falls to the two WeatherTidePanels' role="status" nodes, which mount already containing their text (the unreliable-announcement pattern of prior finding i=74). This is a new location of the exact one-shot-unmount defect of prior finding i=28 (Checklists.tsx:205), in the one component never previously audited. The component's other states pass: the missing-key Nudges are static content with a real, visibly-named 'Go to Settings →' button (line 72) on the passing --sr-warning/--sr-warning-bg pair (6.84:1 light / 15.0:1 dark), and per-side error/unavailable states flow through WeatherTidePanel's verified role="alert"/role="status" markup.
gapFindings.evidence: Line 94-95: `const loadConditions = useCallback(async () => { setLoaded(true); setLoading(true); …`; line 116: `{!keysMissing && !loaded && (` gates the button at 117 `<button tabIndex={0} onClick={() => { void loadConditions() }} disabled={loading}` — `loaded` flips true before the first await, unmounting the focused button; lines 124-125's `loading ? <Loader2…/> : …` / `'Loading…'` are unreachable.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Keep the button mounted through the load: gate it on `!keysMissing && (!loaded || loading)` so the existing disabled 'Loading…' state actually renders and focus is preserved (the dead code becomes live); when the panels replace it on completion, focus is then on a still-mounted disabled control. Alternatively, before unmounting, move focus to the results container (tabIndex={-1} + .focus()), matching the fix direction recorded for finding i=28.

verdict.reasoning: Duplicate of confirmed finding i=28 in verified-findings.json ('One-shot buttons unmount on activation, dropping keyboard focus to <body>') — the code claim is fully accurate (setLoaded(true) at WeatherTideSection.tsx:95 unmounts the button gated by !loaded at :116, making the loading/disabled rendering at :124-125 dead), but it is the identical defect at the identical root cause, just a location i=28's batch omitted, and i=28 explicitly frames itself as the repeated pattern reported once. The only other consequence (loading announced via WeatherTidePanel's mount-with-text role="status" nodes) is likewise already recorded as confirmed pattern finding i=74, which the finding itself acknowledges. Nothing here is a different aspect; it is a location amendment to i=28.
verdict.fixNote: Append WeatherTideSection.tsx:116-117 to i=28's location list when fixing. The finding's local remedy is correct and preferable there: gate the button on !keysMissing && (!loaded || loading) so the existing disabled 'Loading…' rendering becomes live and focus stays on a mounted control until the panels replace it.

gapFindings.title: Multimedia (Life List) filter-count live region announces a wrong total when a county/date filter is active — '0 of 0 species' on a zero-result filter
gapFindings.description: Runtime-verified (Playwright, live app, data loaded): setting the From date to 2099-01-01 made the aria-live="polite" count region (LifeList.tsx:675) announce '0 of 0 species', telling a screen-reader (and sighted) user the dataset is empty rather than that the active filter matched nothing. Root cause: `const totalSpecies = displayEntries.length` (line 436) — but the `displayEntries` memo (lines 276-300) ALREADY applies the county/date location filter, so the denominator collapses with the numerator whenever a location/date filter is active (any nonzero case is equally wrong, e.g. '12 of 12 species' while hundreds exist). BreedingCodeList does this correctly — its denominator is the unfiltered `phaseData!.entries.length` (BreedingCodeList.tsx:243), which announced '0 of 92 species' in the same test.
gapFindings.evidence: Observed live-region text under From=2099-01-01: `{"live":"polite","text":"0 of 0 species"}` (Multimedia) vs `"0 of 92 species"` (Breeding Codes). Code: LifeList.tsx:436-439 `const totalSpecies = displayEntries.length; const countLabel = … : `${filteredCount} of ${totalSpecies} species``, where displayEntries is built from `rawEbirdObs.filter(o => { …countyFilter… dateRange… })` at lines 281-289.
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Compute the denominator from the unfiltered entry set (e.g. `phaseEntries.length`, or the pre-location-filter base list built with the same showSpuh/showNonBird/mergeSubspecies display options), mirroring BreedingCodeList.tsx:243, so the count label always reads 'X of <true total> species'.

verdict.reasoning: Code-verified: LifeList.tsx:436 sets totalSpecies = displayEntries.length, but the displayEntries memo (lines 276-304) already applies the county/date filter, so the aria-live count at line 675 reads '0 of 0 species' (or 'N of N') whenever a location/date filter is active. BreedingCodeList.tsx:243 uses the unfiltered phaseData!.entries.length, confirming the in-house correct pattern. Not present in verified-findings.json or structure-findings.json (i=70 is a different live-region issue).
verdict.fixNote: When an eBird backbone is loaded, the correct unfiltered denominator is the comprehensive base (buildComprehensiveEntries(rawEbirdObs, rawRows, mergeSubspecies)) with the same showSpuh/showNonBird filtering applied — phaseEntries.length alone is the ML-only entry count and undercounts in backbone mode. The suggestedFix's second option is the right one; also reuse it in filterStripText (line 447), which has the same collapsed denominator.

gapFindings.evidence: Runtime probe on both tabs with From=2099-01-01: `{"tableRows":0, "tablePresent":true, "emptyMsg":[]}`; Checklists in the same state showed `"emptyMsg":["No checklists match these filters."]` plus the announced count '0 of 3,163 checklists'.

verdict.fixNote: Minor line correction: BreedingCodeTable's tbody is at lines 164-165, not ~253. Suggested fix is convention-compliant (--sr-text-muted exists in both themes); a full-width <td colSpan={...}> inside the tbody keeps the table structure valid.

gapFindings.title: The 'loading-saved' phase on four data tabs is a bare unlabeled spinner — nothing is announced and nothing names the state
gapFindings.wcag: 4.1.3 Status Messages AA (also 1.1.1 Non-text Content A)
gapFindings.description: While a tab parses the stored CSV (the phase every visit passes through before the data or the SetupRequired panel appears), four tabs replace their entire panel with a centered Loader2 SVG and nothing else: Checklists.tsx:468-470 (the icon is even explicitly aria-hidden, leaving zero accessible content in the panel), LifeList.tsx:362-364, SpeciesDetail.tsx:408-410, and BreedingCodeList.tsx:174-176. There is no role="status", no aria-label, and no visible text, so a screen-reader user lands in an empty tabpanel with no indication anything is happening. Every other loading state in the app does this correctly and was recorded as a pass (boot skeleton role=status 'Loading SnowRaven', App.tsx TabLoading role=status with text, BirdingStats.tsx:464 computing status, SnowMap style placeholder) — these four bare spinners are the stragglers. Distinct from prior finding i=74 (which covers role=status nodes that mount with text already present — these have no status semantics at all).
gapFindings.evidence: Checklists.tsx:469 `<Loader2 size={24} strokeWidth={2} className="spin" style={{ color: 'var(--sr-accent)' }} aria-hidden />` as the sole child of the phase's wrapper div; identical Loader2-only blocks at LifeList.tsx:363, SpeciesDetail.tsx:409, BreedingCodeList.tsx:~176 (those three without even aria-hidden, but with no text either).
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Give each wrapper div role="status" and an aria-label (e.g. 'Loading saved eBird data') — or add visible text next to the spinner as WeatherTidePanel does ('Loading weather…') — and keep the SVG aria-hidden, matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern.

verdict.reasoning: All four cited blocks verified: Checklists.tsx:466-472 (Loader2 with aria-hidden as the panel's sole content), LifeList.tsx:360-366, SpeciesDetail.tsx:406-412, BreedingCodeList.tsx:172-178 — no role='status', no aria-label, no text, leaving an empty tabpanel during the loading-saved phase every visit passes through. Genuinely distinct from confirmed i=74, which covers nodes that already have role='status' but mount with text present; these have no status semantics at all. Not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md and not present in either findings file.
verdict.fixNote: Matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern (role='status' + label on the wrapper, SVG aria-hidden) is right; note per confirmed finding i=74 that a status node mounting with its label may still not be announced by all SRs, but it at least names the state for users who land in the panel — fixing both together would mean mounting the empty status container first and inserting the label.

gapFindings.title: Rotate/pitch gestures left enabled on all four maps with the compass reset hidden — multipoint-only on touch, no single-pointer alternative or reset, and the app never uses bearing/pitch
gapFindings.description: SnowMap's single MapGL mount (SnowMap.tsx:117) passes no gesture overrides, so maplibre-gl 5.24.0 defaults leave dragRotate, touchZoomRotate (rotation), touchPitch, and pitchWithRotate all enabled — empirically confirmed (handler state dragRotateEnabled/touchPitchEnabled/touchZoomRotateEnabled all true in both embed configs; Shift+ArrowRight rotated bearing to 15°, Shift+ArrowUp pitched to 10°). On touch devices, rotation is a two-finger twist and pitch a two-finger vertical drag — multipoint gestures with no single-pointer alternative: the NavigationControl compass (the standard single-tap bearing/pitch reset) is explicitly hidden (`showCompass={false}`, SnowMap.tsx:125), and no app code ever calls resetNorth/setBearing/setPitch. A touch user who triggers these accidentally is stranded in a rotated/tilted view: the app's fitBounds calls reset bearing only — pitch survives fitBounds (verified empirically: pitch 40° unchanged after fitBounds) — and they are data-driven fits, not user-invocable resets. Desktop right-drag/Ctrl-drag and keyboard Shift+arrows exist but are unavailable to touch single-pointer users. The app itself never uses bearing or pitch, so this is unused functionality left armed on all four map surfaces (Map Explorer, Species Detail, Statistics, SightingsMap/Named Birds). Note: this is distinct from every gesture/keyboard finding already recorded in verified-findings.json (none cover rotation/pitch or the hidden compass).
gapFindings.evidence: SnowMap.tsx:125 `<NavigationControl position="top-left" showCompass={false} />`; grep of frontend/src finds no dragRotate/touchPitch/touchZoomRotate/pitchWithRotate/keyboard props on any mount; maplibre-gl src/ui/map.ts:472-499 defaults `dragRotate: true, touchZoomRotate: true, touchPitch: true, pitchWithRotate: true`; live check: bearing 15°/pitch 10° reached via gestures' keyboard twins, and fitBounds left pitch at 40° (bearing-only reset); no resetNorth/setBearing/setPitch anywhere in app code
gapFindings.suggestedFix: Disable the unused gestures once in SnowMap (covers all four surfaces): pass `dragRotate={false}` `touchPitch={false}` `pitchWithRotate={false}` on the MapGL mount, and call `e.target.touchZoomRotate.disableRotation()` in the map's load handler (this keeps pinch ZOOM working — do not pass `touchZoomRotate={false}`, which would disable pinch zoom too). Do NOT call `map.keyboard.disableRotation()` — in maplibre 5.24 it disables keyboard PAN as well as rotate. Alternative if rotation is ever wanted: restore the compass (`showCompass` default) with `visualizePitch: true` so one tap resets bearing and pitch, providing the single-pointer alternative/reset.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: SnowMap.tsx:117-125 passes no gesture overrides (maplibre-gl 5.24 bundle defaults dragRotate/touchZoomRotate/touchPitch/pitchWithRotate all true), hides the compass (showCompass={false}), and grep of frontend/src finds no resetNorth/setBearing/setPitch anywhere — so rotation/pitch are multipoint-only on touch with no single-pointer alternative or reset, on all four SnowMap-backed surfaces. A touch user who accidentally twists/tilts has no recovery control, which is a fair 2.5.1 failure plus a real stranding hazard; no existing finding in either file covers rotation/pitch or the hidden compass.
